column1: # The metaprogramming coverage manifest. Every Jai metaprogramming peer
# family J01 to J40 names the Jet witnesses that prove Jet's answer to it,
# and every row of the public metadata contract
# witness. check.jet runs every witness on its tiers through
# `jet test Compiler --profile corpora` and fails on a family with no row, a
# contract row that is Owed, or a witness that is missing, fails, is skipped
# or did not run on one of its tiers.
# Jai behavior is evidence, not a guarantee. A `source` row says which kind
# - historical: a dated demo or Q&A by the language's author; it shows what
#   an old build did, with no release named.
# - observed: a pinned community source written against a working compiler
#   (a guide, wiki or module at a fixed revision); it shows behavior seen in
#   use, still with no owner release named.
# A family row lists its historical and its observed sources in separate
# columns, so a family that only an old demo shows is never read as current
# Jai behavior; `-` is an empty column.

column7: `#run` evaluates ordinary Jet while building and bakes the value in
a value waits for the pass that makes what it reads; a marker reads the types another marker generates
`#phase` names the phase of the copy that runs it
module values computed while building are frozen into the program; no mutable state crosses phases
`#if` keeps one branch
`#run use` imports for build-time code; members build in dependency order
`meta.add(code, scope:)` adds checked code; a type from text needs `Meta.Code.Types` and `Meta.Code.Raw`

column3: First-class Code values and Code↔AST conversion
column7: `#code { … }` is a `Code` value with typed holes; the parser API reads source as syntax
no macros: a `Code` value captures no free name and has no textual expansion
`#loop` unrolls inside a generated body; inserted code is checked again in place
`#caller` and `#here` give typed call-site facts, never the caller's syntax tree
a generic branches on its type parameter; a specialization's types are checked
`T.reflect()` is the declared type's TypeInfo; `reflect.of(x)` reads a value at run time

markers are typed structs a declaration carries; `M.reflect().uses` lists their uses
`reflect.of(x)` reflects a value with its type all the way down
reflection folds while building; a program keeps only the records it reads
generics specialize per type and per scalar argument
